rv.q: 'Nice Fish' is a whimsical, ultimately resonant portrait of lost souls waiting to hook or be hooked...It’s all vaguely 'Waiting for Godot'–ish, and Jenkins makes a modest bid as a flyover-state Samuel Beckett. Generally, though, the ultimate lure is a chance to see a great actor like Rylance cutting loose.
The whole may not add up to much more than a gently absurdist evocation of mood.
It's not much of a play, to be honest, but as a chance to relish the sublime eccentric charms of Rylance at his best, it's a hoot.
